title: STEM Orchestrator: Managing Multi-hardware-component STEM Automation Seamlessly
content: Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (STEM) plays a crucial role in materials science by providing atomic-resolution imaging, spectroscopy, and diffraction capabilities [1]. However, a significant challenge in modern STEM environments is the lack of cross-communication between various Third-party hardware and software APIs, limiting researchers' ability to accomplish machine learning (ML) based complex automated workflows and venturing in to In-Situ experiments. Thus, there is a need for a community effort to build and maintain a software ecosystem to write server control (if not provided from manufacturers) and connect them together. The STEM Orchestrator is a cutting-edge automation framework that seamlessly integrates different STEM hardware and software components, streamlining high-throughput and reproducible experimentation. Its core objective is to simplify the creation, execution, and sharing of workflows, fostering a collaborative research environment.
